info.text:
Your student loan can still charge interest on its own interest.

It's called capitalization: unpaid interest is added to your principal.
New undergrad Direct Loans (July 2026 to June 2027) carry a fixed 6.52%.
Hypothetical: $10,000 at 6.52%, no payments for 4 years, simple interest adds $2,608. If that interest capitalizes, say at consolidation, yearly interest goes from $652 to about $822.
Since July 2023, Direct Loans no longer capitalize when you enter repayment or leave forbearance; consolidation, some deferments ending and leaving IBR (older loans) still trigger it.

Sources: US Department of Education (Federal Register, Nov 2022; FSA, June 2026), studentaid.gov.
News and education, not financial advice.
